At the highest dose (24 mg), enicepatide achieved a mean HbA1c reduction of 2.65% at 48 weeks, highlighting its potential for best-in-disease glycemic control
In patients with poor baseline glycemic control (HbA1c >8.5%), enicepatide 24 mg led to an HbA1c reduction of 4.13% at 48 weeks
By week 48, 90% of patients in the 24 mg enicepatide arm met the T2D glycemic target of ≤6.5% HbA1c, while 62% achieved normoglycemia (HbA1c < 5.7%)
At the highest 24 mg dose, enicepatide achieved a mean weight loss of 15.5% at 48 weeks, without a weight loss plateau
Enicepatide demonstrated a safety and tolerability profile consistent with the incretin class, with low discontinuation rates and no new safety signals identified
